page: Amazon Web Services r5n.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz, providing 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core workloads. Single-core processing, evaluated via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the lower 25% tier. However, multi-core execution, memory bandwidth, and database operations like Redis SET scale to average levels, placing in the middle 50% of tested systems. The instance achieves a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps, supporting efficient data transfer for network-bound tasks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r5n.4xlarge offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio suitable for memory-intensive workloads without the premium of local NVMe drives. Given its hardware profile and average multi-core and memory bandwidth performance, this instance is suited for memory-cached databases, enterprise applications, and mid-sized data processing tasks that do not require high single-threaded compute performance.
